comparison: Both strongly support the core finding that basepairing status affects substitution frequencies (C2, C3, C25-C40). OpenEval emphasizes the statistical rigor (Tukey's test, Bonferroni correction, bootstrapped confidence intervals), while peer reviewers affirm the finding is 'valuable and convincing' with no challenges to the statistical analysis or effect magnitudes.

Both address context-dependent effects (C45-C52). OpenEval finds these claims supported with quantitative confidence intervals. Peer reviewers initially questioned why sequence context wasn't investigated, but after revision stated 'the revisions have addressed my main comments' and 'the additional analysis strengthens the conclusions,' indicating acceptance of these findings.

Both address secondary structure model comparisons (C58-C62) and DMS reactivity analysis (C53-C55, C63-C64). OpenEval finds the analysis appropriately cautious. Peer reviewers raise significant methodological concerns about the DMS dataset (MOI, timepoint, synchronicity, degradation artifacts) leading to UNCERTAIN evaluation, though they acknowledge limitations are addressed.

OpenEval R4 addresses correlation analyses with DMS reactivity (C53-C57), while peer R3 raises concerns about the DMS dataset quality affecting these correlations. OpenEval finds the reduced correlation for nonsynonymous substitutions appropriately attributed to fitness effects, but peer reviewers note dynamic positions may impact fitness estimations.

OpenEval R6 discusses the C29095 case study (C63-C65) demonstrating value of continuous DMS reactivity data. This overlaps with peer R3's concerns about DMS data quality, though peer reviewers ultimately accepted the revisions while acknowledging methodological limitations remain.

Both address the basepairing adjustment method (C66-C73). OpenEval finds the coarse adjustment appropriately validated with clear quantification. Peer reviewers support this approach, noting 'the conclusions of this work are generally well supported' and accepting it as a 'first-order approximation' with acknowledged limitations.

Both address identification of lineage-defining mutations through basepairing adjustment (C74-C82). OpenEval finds the hypothesis testing and quantitative results support the conclusion. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this demonstrates 'the importance of considering RNA secondary structure in viral evolution studies' with no challenges to the findings.

Both discuss the C29095T case study and its biological significance (C83-C90). OpenEval finds the historical context and citations appropriate. Peer reviewers support this as part of the broader demonstration that is 'valuable and convincing,' highlighting importance of studying mutational fitness beyond immune evasion.

Both address extension to G→U substitutions (C91-C93). OpenEval finds this provides additional validation across substitution types. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the systematic demonstration they describe as valuable, with no specific objections to the G→U analysis.

Both address conceptual framing and limitations regarding mutation vs. selection (C94-C97). OpenEval finds the distinctions and acknowledgment of phylogenetic limitations appropriate. Peer reviewers affirm the broader implications and accept the suggestions for future work without objection.

Both address mechanistic interpretations (C98-C106). OpenEval finds the contrast between interpretations appropriately presented with appropriate uncertainty. Peer reviewers note the work 'raises novel mechanistic questions' and initially criticized lack of mechanistic insights, but after revision stated concerns were addressed.

Both address the G→U mechanism hypothesis (C104-C106). OpenEval finds the parallel between C→U and G→U strengthens the hypothesis while remaining appropriately speculative. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the novel mechanistic questions raised by the study.

Both address suggestions for future work and data integration (C107-C113). OpenEval finds these appropriately framed as suggestions rather than demonstrated results. Peer reviewers affirm the methods 'can be readily implemented in existing datasets' and describe the work as presenting 'clear methods and an easy-to-access bioinformatic pipeline.'

Both address caveats and future directions (C114-C119). OpenEval finds the acknowledgment of in vitro vs. in vivo differences and emphasis on uncertainty evaluation demonstrate scientific rigor. Peer reviewers accept these broader implications and suggestions without objection.

Both address methodological transparency and limitations (C124-C134, C126-C133 overlap). OpenEval finds the documentation of limitations strengthens confidence despite acknowledged issues. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'the author acknowledges most limitations of the analyses and addresses them' and ultimately conclude concerns were addressed after revision.

Minor overlap on in vitro limitations (C116). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the acknowledgment of this limitation appropriate, with peer reviewers noting the author addresses limitations adequately.

OpenEval R17 addresses definitions and main hypothesis (C4-C7, C22-C24), with minor overlap on C6-C7 with peer R5. OpenEval finds the hypothesis supported by subsequent results. Peer reviewers affirm the systematic demonstration of this hypothesis as 'valuable and convincing.'

OpenEval R1 addresses data sources and citations (C1, C120-C123). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these methodological documentation claims, though peer reviewers generally accepted the methods.

OpenEval R18 addresses the motivating case study and literature review (C8-C21). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these background and motivation claims, though the rationale was implicitly accepted.

OpenEval R19 addresses independent validation citations (C41-C44). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these validation claims from other studies, though convergence with independent work strengthens the findings.
